CALIFORNIA FEE-CHARGING EMPLOYMENT AGENCY REGULATION — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme Career Placement, Inc.

DECLARATION AND PURPOSE
This information sheet concerns a fee-charging employment agency relationship involving Jordan Lee (the "jobseeker") and Acme Career Placement, Inc., identified here as an employment agency for reference only. This sheet summarizes provisions of California's Employment Agency, Employment Counseling, and Job Listing Services Act, Civil Code section 1812.500 et seq., which regulates businesses that charge a jobseeker -- rather than only an employer -- a fee to help the jobseeker find work. It is a distinct statute from California's Talent Agencies Act, Labor Code section 1700 et seq., which governs procuring engagements for artists in the entertainment industry.

WHO IS A FEE-CHARGING "EMPLOYMENT AGENCY": STATUTORY DEFINITION
California's Employment Agency, Employment Counseling, and Job Listing Services Act defines who is regulated as an "employment agency" under Civil Code section 1812.503 et seq. Civil Code section 1812.501(a)(1)(A) defines an "employment agency" or "agency" to include any person who, for a fee or other valuable consideration paid directly or indirectly by a jobseeker, procures, offers, promises, or attempts to procure employment for others, registers persons seeking employment, gives information about where employment may be procured, or provides employment. Section 1812.501(e) separately defines "jobseeker" to mean a person seeking employment.

The statute distinguishes an "employment agency" from two related, separately regulated categories that Civil Code section 1812.501(a)(2) expressly excludes from the "employment agency" definition: an "employment counseling service" (career counseling, résumé preparation, and similar services, defined in section 1812.501(b)) and a "job listing service" (defined in section 1812.501(c)). Whether Acme Career Placement, Inc.'s services fall within the "employment agency" definition, the "employment counseling service" definition, the "job listing service" definition, or none of them is a fact this sheet does not state.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Any person who, for a fee or other valuable consideration to be paid, directly or indirectly by a jobseeker, performs, offers to perform, or represents it can or will perform any of the following services:"
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 1812.501(a)(1)(A), Civil Code § 1812.501(a)(1)(A) (definition of "employment agency") (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1812.501)
  "“Jobseeker” means a person seeking employment."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 1812.501(e), Civil Code § 1812.501(e) (definition of "jobseeker") (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1812.501)
  Known gap: Civil Code section 1812.501 was fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov as separate HTTP requests using two distinct User-Agent headers; both retrievals returned byte-identical text for the full section after whitespace normalization. This clause relies on a single statutory section for both quoted definitions, so no source-independence disclosure beyond that dual-fetch consistency check applies. This clause states only the statutory definitions; it does not determine which category, if any, a given business falls into, and it does not address section 1812.501(d)'s separate treatment of a "nurses' registry" as an employment agency governed by a different chapter (Chapter 7, commencing with section 1812.524) rather than the Chapter 2 provisions (bonding, fee limits, prohibited practices) this document otherwise summarizes.

SURETY BOND REQUIREMENT
California does not require a fee-charging employment agency to hold a Labor-Commissioner-issued license comparable to the Talent Agencies Act's license. Instead, Civil Code section 1812.503(a) requires every employment agency subject to the Act to maintain a surety bond, in a principal sum of $3,000, issued by a surety company admitted to do business in California, with a copy filed with the Secretary of State. Section 1812.503(b) states that the bond is payable to the people of the State of California and exists for the benefit of any person damaged by a violation of the Act or by the agency's fraud, dishonesty, misrepresentation, or failure to provide the contracted services.

Section 1812.503(c)(1) states that no employment agency may conduct business without a current bond on file. The statute also permits a cash deposit filed with the Secretary of State in lieu of a bond, under a claims procedure the same section describes.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Every employment agency subject to this title shall maintain a bond issued by a surety company admitted to do business in this state. The principal sum of the bond shall be three thousand dollars ($3,000). A copy of the bond shall be filed with the Secretary of State."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 1812.503(a), Civil Code § 1812.503(a) (surety bond requirement) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1812.503)
  "No employment agency shall conduct any business without having a current surety bond in the amount prescribed by this title and filing a copy of the bond with the Secretary of State."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 1812.503(c)(1), Civil Code § 1812.503(c)(1) (no business without a current bond) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1812.503)
  Known gap: Civil Code section 1812.503 was fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov as separate HTTP requests using two distinct User-Agent headers; both retrievals returned byte-identical text for the full section after whitespace normalization. This clause draws on one statutory section only, so it is not independently corroborated by a second source. This clause states the bonding requirement's existence and dollar amount as of the version of section 1812.503 currently posted on leginfo; it does not confirm whether any particular employment agency in fact maintains a bond or deposit on file with the Secretary of State, and it does not address section 1812.501(d)'s separate rule that a nurses' registry, though itself an "employment agency," is not required to comply with this bonding chapter and instead follows Chapter 7 (commencing with section 1812.524).

JOBSEEKER FEE SCHEDULE, DISCLOSURE, AND LIMITS
California law imposes disclosure and dollar limits on what a fee-charging employment agency may charge a jobseeker. Civil Code section 1812.505(a)(1) requires an employment agency to provide a copy of its jobseeker fee schedule and payment terms to any jobseeker from whom a fee or deposit is to be received, before the jobseeker is interviewed by a counselor, and requires the fee schedule to indicate the percentage of projected earnings the fee represents. Section 1812.505(a)(3) further requires the current fee schedule to be posted in a conspicuous place in the agency's office.

Section 1812.505(b) states that no fee charged or collected may exceed the fee as scheduled, and section 1812.505(c) separately prohibits an employment agency from accepting a registration fee of any kind. The same section also caps a jobseeker's total fee exposure: under section 1812.505(f)(3), in no case where the accepted employment is later terminated may the fee charged to the jobseeker exceed the jobseeker's total gross earnings from that employment.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "An employment agency shall provide a copy of the agency’s jobseeker fee schedule and payment terms to any jobseeker from whom a fee or deposit is to be received, prior to the jobseeker being interviewed by a counselor."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 1812.505(a)(1), Civil Code § 1812.505(a)(1) (fee schedule disclosure) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1812.505)
  "No fee charged or collected shall be in excess of the fee as scheduled."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 1812.505(b), Civil Code § 1812.505(b) (no fee above the posted schedule) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1812.505)
  "No employment agency shall accept, directly or indirectly, a registration fee of any kind."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 1812.505(c), Civil Code § 1812.505(c) (no registration fee) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1812.505)
  Known gap: Civil Code section 1812.505 was fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov as separate HTTP requests using two distinct User-Agent headers; both retrievals returned byte-identical text for the full section after whitespace normalization. All three quotations below come from this single section, so this clause is not corroborated by an independent source. This clause states the fee-schedule disclosure requirement and the two flat prohibitions (no above-schedule fee, no registration fee) it quotes directly; it summarizes rather than quotes section 1812.505(f)(3)'s gross-earnings cap and the section's further provisions on temporary-employment fee proration, commission-based fee computation, and interagency fee disputes, which this clause does not otherwise cover. It does not state what fee schedule, if any, any particular employment agency has posted or provided.

REFUND WHERE THE JOBSEEKER DOES NOT ACCEPT EMPLOYMENT
California law addresses what happens to a fee or deposit a jobseeker has paid, or become obligated to pay, if the jobseeker does not accept the employment the agency arranged. Civil Code section 1812.506(a) states that in that circumstance, the employment agency must, upon the jobseeker's request, repay the deposit or fee, and if the repayment is not made within 48 hours of the request, the agency must additionally pay the jobseeker a sum equal to the amount of the deposit.

Section 1812.506(c)(1) separately requires that, except as otherwise addressed in subdivision (a), any refund due must be made within 10 working days of the jobseeker's request, or the agency must notify the jobseeker in writing of the specific reasons a refund is not being made.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "If a jobseeker paying or becoming obligated to pay a fee, or making a deposit on a fee for placement fails to accept employment, the employment agency shall, upon request by the jobseeker, repay the amount of the deposit or fee to the jobseeker. Unless the deposit is returned within 48 hours after request, the employment agency shall pay to the jobseeker an additional sum equal to the amount of the deposit."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 1812.506(a), Civil Code § 1812.506(a) (refund if employment not accepted) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1812.506)
  Known gap: Civil Code section 1812.506 was fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov as separate HTTP requests using two distinct User-Agent headers; both retrievals returned byte-identical text for the full section after whitespace normalization. This clause relies on a single statutory section, so it is not corroborated by an independent source. It quotes only subdivision (a) and summarizes subdivision (c)(1) rather than quoting it; it does not cover subdivision (b)'s separate rules distinguishing a refund or fee reduction for a jobseeker who leaves or is discharged from accepted employment within 90 days, including that subdivision's lists of what counts as "just cause" or "discharge for reasons other than misconduct" versus "misconduct." It does not state whether any refund is currently due between any particular jobseeker and employment agency.

PROHIBITED PRACTICES: NONEXISTENT JOBS AND FALSE REPRESENTATIONS
California law specifically prohibits an employment agency from referring a jobseeker to work on the basis of a job order the agency has reason to know does not check out. Civil Code section 1812.507(c) states that an employment agency may not refer a jobseeker to a job knowing or having reason to know that the job does not exist or the jobseeker is not qualified for it, or that the job has been described or advertised by or on behalf of the agency in a false, misleading, or deceptive manner.

A related, more general prohibition reaches advertising and representations to jobseekers as a whole. Civil Code section 1812.508(a) states that an employment agency may not make, or cause to be made, any false, misleading, or deceptive advertisements or representations concerning the services the agency will provide to jobseekers, and section 1812.508(b)(4) separately prohibits an employment agency from giving false information or making false promises or representations concerning an engagement or employment to any jobseeker who registers or applies for one.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "No employment agency shall refer a jobseeker to a job knowing or having reason to know that: (1) The job does not exist or the jobseeker is not qualified for the job. (2) The job has been described or advertised by or on behalf of the agency in a false, misleading, or deceptive manner."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 1812.507(c), Civil Code § 1812.507(c) (no referral to a job known to be nonexistent or falsely described) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1812.507)
  "No employment agency shall make, or cause to be made, any false, misleading, or deceptive advertisements or representations concerning the services that the agency will provide to jobseekers."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 1812.508(a), Civil Code § 1812.508(a) (no false, misleading, or deceptive advertisements or representations) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1812.508)
  "No employment agency shall give any false information or make any false promises or representations concerning an engagement or employment to any jobseeker who registers or applies for an engagement or employment or help."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 1812.508(b)(4), Civil Code § 1812.508(b)(4) (no false information or promises to a registering jobseeker) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1812.508)
  Known gap: Civil Code sections 1812.507 and 1812.508 were each fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov as separate HTTP requests using two distinct User-Agent headers; all four retrievals returned byte-identical text for their respective full sections after whitespace normalization. Sections 1812.507 and 1812.508 independently prohibit overlapping conduct (misrepresenting a job's existence or description), which corroborates that this is a settled feature of the statute rather than an artifact of a single section's drafting; beyond that, this clause is not corroborated by case law or a source outside the statute itself. It quotes only the specific job-order and advertising prohibitions above; it does not cover section 1812.508's separate, detailed rules on "FEE"/"NO FEE" advertisement labeling, salary-advertisement formatting, or the home-health-agency representation restriction, and it does not state whether any specific job referral, advertisement, or statement by any particular employment agency complied with these provisions.

RECORD AND SIGNATURE
Jordan Lee and Acme Career Placement, Inc. identify the following as of the date this sheet is completed:

Jobseeker: Jordan Lee
Employment agency: Acme Career Placement, Inc.
Date: September 5, 2026
Location: Oakland, California

This sheet is an informational record only. It is not the written contract that Civil Code section 1812.504 requires an employment agency to give a jobseeker, a posted fee schedule under Civil Code section 1812.505, a surety bond filing with the Secretary of State under Civil Code section 1812.503, or a waiver of any right or requirement under Civil Code section 1812.500 et seq.
